x: বইটির উদ্দেশ্য · What this book is for এই বইয়ের দুটি লক্ষ্য: চাইনিজ শেখা, একদম শূন্য থেকে HSK 4: উচ্চারণ, টোন ও অক্ষর লেখা (Part 0), শব্দভান্ডার, ব্যাকরণ, অডিও QR কোড দিয়ে শোনা, Practice Ladder দিয়ে বলা, আর Appendix D-তে HSK পরীক্ষার গাইড। পূর্ণাঙ্গ, বৈধ ও বন্ধুত্বভিত্তিক দাওয়াত: কেন আল্লাহয় বিশ্বাস করব, প্রমাণ, আপত্তির উত্তর, চীনের প্রেক্ষাপট, আর তৈরি কথোপকথন। প্রতিটা চাইনিজ বাক্যের সাথে পিনইন, ইংরেজি ও বাংলা অর্থ আছে, আর প্রতিটা অংশ শেষ হয় একটা বাংলা সারকথা দিয়ে। This book has two goals: Learn Chinese from zero to HSK 4: pronunciation, tones and characters (Part 0), vocabulary, grammar, listening with the audio QR codes, speaking with the Practice Ladder, and the HSK exam guide in Appendix D. Carry out complete, lawful, friendship-based dawah: why believe, the evidence, answers to objections, the China context, and ready-made conversations. Every Chinese sentence has pinyin, English and Bengali, and every section ends with a Bengali summary. This book was written for a Muslim living in China who wants to answer two kinds of questions: the questions of people who do not believe in God, and the questions Chinese people ask about Islam. It was also written for someone still learning Chinese, so the language is taught alongside the message. Three convictions shaped it. First, truth does not need exaggeration: every piece of evidence in this book is graded, and claims that careful Muslim scholars themselves reject have been left out or marked. Second, character comes before argument: most people are moved by a trustworthy friend long before they are moved by a proof. Third, China is not foreign soil for Islam: Muslims have lived here since 651, and Chinese Muslim scholars explained Islam in the language of Confucius more than three centuries ago. This book follows their path. It is a working edition. Before you print or teach from it, ask a qualified scholar to review the religious content and a native Chinese speaker to review the Chinese (see the pre-publication checklist in Appendix B). সারকথা: বইটি চীনে থাকা একজন মুসলিমের জন্য, যে নাস্তিক ও চীনা বন্ধুদের প্রশ্নের উত্তর দিতে চায় আর একই সাথে চাইনিজ শিখছে। তিনটি নীতি: সত্যে অতিরঞ্জন নেই, যুক্তির আগে চরিত্র, আর চীন ইসলামের জন্য অপরিচিত মাটি নয়।

h:
From zero to HSK 4: a
one-year path
x: What this book can do, and what it cannot do alone. It can teach you the sounds and tones, how characters work, the 1,089 HSK 1–4 words, the grammar of each level and the HSK exam format. It can give you dawah language at every level, and audio for every Chinese word in it. It cannot hear you. No book can correct your tones or your speaking, so you also need a teacher or a language partner. For full HSK exam practice, add the official sample papers and a mock test before each exam. If you can, study alongside a Chinese class or the standard HSK textbooks. This book then becomes the place where your Chinese and your dawah meet. সৎ কথা: এই বই দিয়ে একদম শূন্য থেকে শুরু করে HSK 4 পর্যন্ত যাওয়া যায়, আর প্রতিটা লেভেলে দাওয়াহর ভাষা শেখা যায়। কিন্তু বই তোমার উচ্চারণ শুনতে পারে না। তাই সপ্তাহে অন্তত একবার একজন শিক্ষক বা ভাষা-সঙ্গীর ( 语伴 ) সাথে কথা বলো, আর প্রতিটা পরীক্ষার আগে একটা mock test দাও। Months Level Learn Chinese (book) Dawah skill App Exam 1 Zero to HSK 1 Part 0; VI.2 Tier 1; VI.3; D.2 Introduce yourself, ask for halal food, excuse yourself to pray (VI.8, scenario 1) HSK 1 tab;  Dawah stages 1, 2, 5 HSK 1 (optional) 2–3 HSK 2 VI.4; D.3; C.2 Answer Q1–Q6 at HSK 2; scenarios 2–3 HSK 2 tab;  Dawah stages 6, 9, 10 HSK 2 at the end of month 3 4–6 HSK 3 VI.5; D.4; Part V, Lessons 1–6; Appendix A Explain one God, the hereafter and Ramadan; all 12 questions at HSK 3; scenarios 4–6 HSK 3 tab;  Dawah stages 3, 7, 11 HSK 3 in month 6 7–12 HSK 4 VI.6; D.5; Part V, Lessons 7–12; read the Chinese lines of Part I Short arguments; Q4–Q12 at HSK 4; scenarios 7–8; the one-minute message (7.4) HSK 4 tab;  Dawah stages 4, 8, 12, 13 HSK 4 in month 12 Every week. h:
Disclaimer, legal
note and scholarly review
x: Not a fatwa. This book summarises what established Muslim scholars and institutions have written; it is not a ruling. On any question of belief or practice, follow a qualified scholar. Not legal advice. Part I, Chapter 1 and Part IV, section 4 summarise the published rules on foreigners' religious activity in China as of October 2026. Rules and their enforcement change; check them yourself. This book is for your own study. Do not copy, print or distribute it to Chinese citizens, and do not post its content on Chinese platforms. Chinese language. The Chinese was prepared for a learner and has not yet been checked by a native speaker. Have a Chinese Muslim or teacher correct it before you rely on it in public. Quran and hadith. Check every Chinese verse against Ma Jian's printed translation and every hadith number at sunnah.com before quoting. Humility. If anything in this book is correct, it is from God; any error is from its compilers. Corrections are welcome and will be added to the next edition. সারকথা: এই বই ফতোয়া নয়, আইনি পরামর্শও নয়। এটা নিজের পড়ার জন্য: চীনা নাগরিকদের মধ্যে বিতরণ বা চীনা প্ল্যাটফর্মে পোস্ট কোরো না, আর ব্যবহারের আগে আলেম ও চীনা ভাষাভাষীকে দিয়ে যাচাই করিয়ে নাও।

Listen to this section · শুনুন Characters, not letters. Each character ( 汉字 hànzì) is one syllable and usually one meaning: 人 rén "person", 水 shuǐ "water". Most words have one or two characters: 学生 xuéshēng "student". Pinyin is the Latin spelling of the sound. You learn to speak with pinyin and to read with characters. Every Chinese sentence in this book has both. Tones. Every syllable has a pitch pattern, and the tone changes the meaning: mā 妈 "mother", mǎ 马 "horse". There are four tones and a light "neutral" tone. No grammar endings. Verbs never change: 我去 wǒ qù "I go", 他去 tā qù "he goes", 我昨天去了 "I went yesterday". Word order and small words such as 了 , 吗 and 的 do the work. Simplified characters. Mainland China uses simplified characters ( 汉 rather than 漢 ). This book uses them throughout. সারকথা: চাইনিজে বর্ণমালা নেই, প্রতিটা অক্ষর একটা শব্দাংশ। উচ্চারণ শেখো pinyin দিয়ে, পড়া শেখো অক্ষর দিয়ে। টোন বদলালে অর্থ বদলায়, কিন্তু ক্রিয়ার রূপ কখনো বদলায় না।

Listen to this section · শুনুন A pinyin syllable = initial (the first consonant) + final (the rest) + tone . In mā , the initial is m, the final is a and the tone is the first tone. The table compares each initial with the nearest Bengali sound. The most important column is the second one: b, d, g, j, zh and z are NOT voiced like Bengali ব, দ, গ, জ. They are plain unbreathed sounds, like প, ত, ক, চ. Their partners p, t, k, q, ch and c are the breathy ones, like ফ (with the lips), থ, খ, ছ. Listen to this section · শুনুন Tone Mark Pitch How to feel it in Bengali Example 汉字 Meaning 1st ā high and level singing one long note: "আ———" mā 妈 mother 2nd á rising a surprised question: "কী?" má 麻 hemp 3rd ǎ low, dipping a doubtful, low "হুঁ…" mǎ 马 horse 4th à falling sharply a short command: "যাও!" mà 骂 to scold neutral a short and light no stress at all ma 吗 (question) Three tone-change rules. Pinyin in this book already shows the changed tone, so you only need to recognise them. Two third tones: the first becomes second. 你好 nǐ + hǎo is said ní hǎo . 不 bù becomes bú before a fourth tone: 不是 bú shì , 不去 bú qù . 一 yī becomes yì before tones 1, 2 and 3 ( 一天 yì tiān) and yí before tone 4 ( 一个 yí ge). When counting or in dates it stays yī. Daily drill (two minutes). Read across the table aloud: mā má mǎ mà ma, then bā bá bǎ bà ba, then the pairs 真主 Zhēnzhǔ / 珍珠 zhēnzhū and 主 zhǔ / 猪 zhū (see VI.10). Chapter 1:
Dawah in China: method, manners and the law
x: Listen to this section · শুনুন 1.1 Who you are speaking to Most Chinese people are not committed atheists. About 10% of Chinese adults formally identify with a religion, yet 47% believe in fengshui and 33% believe in the Buddha or a bodhisattva [1]. Many were taught atheism at school but still speak of fate ( 命 mìng), Heaven ( 天 tiān) and ancestors. Most have never thought seriously about God. Your first task is rarely to defeat atheism; it is to help someone think about the question for the first time. Confucian values (honesty, respect for parents, modesty, family, self-discipline) are close to Islamic values, and Chinese Muslim scholars used them as a bridge 350 years ago [2]. Islam has been in China since 651 CE [3]. You are not bringing something foreign; you are pointing to something already part of China's story. 1.2 The law: what you may and may not do Two sets of rules apply to you as a foreigner: the Regulations on Religious Affairs (in force since 1 February 2018) and the Detailed Rules on the religious activities of foreigners (National Religious Affairs Administration Order No. 23, in force since 1 May 2025) [4]. You may attend a registered mosque, join foreigner-only gatherings at approved venues, bring a few religious books for personal use, and live your faith openly. You may not preach without authorisation, recruit Chinese citizens as followers, distribute or sell religious materials, set up any religious group or class, or post religious content online for Chinese audiences. In practice: build friendships, answer questions people ask you, and when someone is seriously interested, introduce them to the ahong (imam) at a registered mosque. Never discuss Xinjiang or politics. Protect yourself and the people you talk to. Part IV, section 4 gives the details. 1.3 The method of the Quran “Invite to the way of your Lord with wisdom and good instruction, and argue with them in a way that is best” (Quran 16:125). In practice: Friendship first. Share food (halal food is a natural topic), help people, be reliable. Chinese culture trusts people before arguments. Ask questions, do not lecture. “Do you think the universe has a beginning?” works better than a speech. Agree where you can. “Yes, science is important. Islam commands us to study it.” Then add the one point they are missing. One idea per conversation. Leave them with one thing to think about, not twenty. Respect Chinese civilisation. Never mock the Buddha, Confucius or China. Quote Confuc

h:
Chapter 2: Why
believe in God: six arguments
x: Listen to this section · শুনুন You do not need all six. Learn the first two deeply; they are enough for most conversations. The others are for people who push further. The Chinese course teaches these in Lessons 3 and 4. 2.1 The universe began, so it needs a cause Everything that begins to exist has a cause. Nothing comes from nothing. The universe began to exist. Modern cosmology places the beginning of space, time and matter about 13.8 billion years ago, and the Borde-Guth-Vilenkin theorem shows that any universe that has on average been expanding cannot be infinite in the past [1]. Therefore the universe has a cause. That cause is outside space, time and matter: timeless, non-physical, immensely powerful, and it chose to create, because a timeless cause producing a universe that begins in time implies a will. This is what we call God. Quran 52:35-36: “Were they created by nothing, or were they the creators? Or did they create the heavens and the earth? No, they have no certainty.” The three options (from nothing, self-created, created by a Creator) are the whole debate in two verses [2]. 中文 : 宇宙有开始。有开始的东西一定有原因。所以宇宙有一个超越时间和空间的创造者。 (Yǔzhòu yǒu kāishǐ. Yǒu kāishǐ de dōngxi yídìng yǒu yuányīn. Suǒyǐ yǔzhòu yǒu yí ge chāoyuè shíjiān hé kōngjiān de chuàngzàozhě.) “ The universe had a beginning. Whatever begins must have a cause. So the universe has a Creator beyond time and space. ” বাংলা মহাবিশ্বের একটা শুরু আছে। যার শুরু আছে, তার অবশ্যই একটা কারণ আছে। তাই মহাবিশ্বের একজন স্রষ্টা আছেন, যিনি সময় ও স্থানের ঊর্ধ্বে। 2.2 The universe is fine-tuned for life The constants of physics sit inside very narrow ranges. The cosmological constant is often described as tuned to about one part in 10^120; a small change in the strength of the strong nuclear force would prevent the formation of carbon or of stable atoms [3]. There are three explanations: chance, necessity or design. Chance of this size is not a serious answer. Physics does not say the constants had to have these values. Design is the natural reading. The multiverse is the usual escape, but it is unobserved, and a universe-generator would itself need fine-tuning, which moves the problem up one level [4]. Quran 67:3: “You do not see in the creation of the Most Merciful any inconsistency. So return your vision to the sky: do you see any flaw?” 中文 : 物理常数非常精确，稍微改变一点，生命就不可能存在。这不像巧合，更像设计。 (Wùlǐ chángshù fēicháng jīngquè, shāowēi gǎibiàn yìdiǎn, shēngmìng jiù bù kěnéng cúnzài. Zhè bú xiàng qiǎohé, gèng xiàng shèjì

Listen to this section · শুনুন Each answer gives the English explanation, then a short Chinese reply you can say. Part III has 44 objections in more depth. Q1. “ If everything needs a cause, who created God? ” 谁创造了真主？ বাংলা: “আল্লাহকে কে সৃষ্টি করেছে?” The argument never said “everything needs a cause”. It said “everything that begins needs a cause”. God does not begin; He is eternal and outside time. Asking “who created the uncreated?” is like asking “what is north of the North Pole?”. An endless chain of creators is impossible too: if every creator needed a creator, nothing would ever start, like a line of soldiers each waiting for the one behind to fire first. The chain must end in one uncreated Creator [1]. Quran 112:3: “He neither begets nor is born.” 中文 : 我们说的是“有开始的东西需要原因”。真主没有开始，他是永恒的，在时间之外。如果每个创造者都需要创造者，那什么都不会存在。 (Wǒmen shuō de shì “ yǒu kāishǐ de dōngxi xūyào yuányīn ” . Unverified = a quote or figure that circulates in dawah material but could not be traced to a primary source. Do not use it in public until you have checked it. Drop = a popular item that careful Muslim scholars themselves reject or that has been shown false. Leave it out. Honesty rules for using evidence in dawah. These come from the dawah scholars themselves (Hamza Tzortzis's 2013 essay withdrawing the “scientific miracles” approach, Yasir Qadhi's warning that over-reading miracles “makes Muslims look foolish to non-Muslims”, and Yaqeen's apologetics guidelines): Say “consistent with”, not “predicted”. A 7th-century text that makes no demonstrable scientific error is a defensible claim; “the Quran predicted the Big Bang” is not. Use the items whose Arabic is plain in any translation (life from water, embryo stages, deep-sea darkness, two seas, milk, three darknesses). Flag the translation-dependent ones (lowest land, egg-shaped earth, expanding, iron sent down) as “possible readings” or leave them out. Never fight for one example. If a sceptic challenges it, concede and move on. The strength is the pattern. Do not quote the retracted scientist testimonials (Hay, Kroner). Quote Keith Moore only with context. Pair science with the stronger evidences: preservation, the literary challenge, prophecy, the Prophet's character, and the arguments for God in the handbook. The challenge verses: 2:23 and 10:38 (produce one surah like it), 11:13 (ten surahs), 17:88 (humans and jinn together cannot produce its like), 52:33-34. The challenge was issued to the masters of Arabic, who had every motive to answer it, and it was never met. How Hamza Tzortzis presents it (“The Qur'an's Unique Literary Form”; The Divine Reality chapter 13): classical Arabic has two forms, poetry (sixteen metres) and prose (rhymed saj' or plain). The Quran fits neither; it is a new literary form, and the inability of any Arab in 1,400 years to produce its like is the miracle. He stresses this is a claim to be tested by Arabic experts, so for a non-Arab audience it rests on testimony. Literary features commonly cited: Ring composition of Surah 2: Raymond Farrin, The Muslim World 100 (2010) and Structure and Qur'anic Interpretation (2014), finds nine concentric sections mirroring each other around the centre. (The popular claim that verse 2:143 is the exact centre is unverified; cite Farrin's structure, not the verse number.) Surah 55: the refrain “Which of your Lord's favours will you both deny?” occurs 31 times in a precise pattern. Surah 108 (al-Kawthar): ten words, three verses, cited by classical scholars as a complete miracle in miniature; al-Razi disagreed that short surahs carry the challenge. Listen to this section · শুনুন The dawah organisations teach four things before any single argument. 1. Fitrah first. Belief in God is natural, not learned. Yaqeen Institute's case for God (Justin Parrott) rests on signs that reach “ both the heart (via intuition) and the mind (through rational thought) ” : Quran 30:30 (the natural disposition on which God created mankind), 10:22-23 and 29:65 (people call on God alone when the ship is sinking), and the hadith “ every child is born upon the fitrah ” (Bukhari and Muslim). Nazir Khan's paper on Ibn Taymiyyah adds that if you doubt the God-sense you have no principled place to stop before doubting reason and the senses too. In China the fitrah shows in the language: 老天爷 , 谢天谢地 , 天啊 . বাংলা 老天爷 (lǎotiānyé, “ Old Man Heaven ” ) = উপরওয়ালা; 谢天谢地 (xiè tiān xiè dì, “ thank heaven and earth ” ) = যাক, উপরওয়ালার দয়ায় বাঁচা গেল; 天啊 (tiān a, “ Oh heavens! ” ) = হায় আসমান! (আমাদের “ হায় আল্লাহ! ” -এর মতো)। অর্থাৎ চীনা মানুষের মুখের ভাষাতেও স্রষ্টার দিকে স্বাভাবিক টান রয়ে গেছে। 2. The Quran's own argument, 52:35-36. “Were they created by nothing, or were they themselves the creators? Or did they create the heavens and the earth?” Hamza Tzortzis reads this as a complete set of options for anything that began: from nothing (absurd: nothing has no power), self-created (contradiction: you must exist before you act), created by something itself created (leads back to the same question), or created by something uncreated. Only the last stands. Bukhari records that Jubayr ibn Mut'im, still a pagan, heard these verses and “his heart almost began to soar”. 3. The dependency argument (Ibn Sina, al-Ghazali, al-Razi; Tzortzis's “Divine Link”). Everything we see is dependent: it could have not existed and relies on something else. A chain of dependent things, even an infinite one, cannot explain itself, as an infinite row of falling dominoes does not explain why any domino fell. So there must be an independent, necessary, eternal being. This is not a God-of-the-gaps move: it reasons from what we know (dependence), not from what we do not know. Mohammed Hijab's The Burhan (Sapience Institute) develops the same proof. 4. The conversation, not the debate. Yaqeen's apologetics guidelines (Hatem al-Haj): building certainty is “always superior to answering doubts”; “intellectual debates rarely change deeply-held beliefs directly, often masking deeper emotional discontent or social bonds.” iERA's training template, GORAP (God's exi

A1. “Who created God?” A category error: “who made X?” applies only to things that began or depend on something. The dependency argument ends in a being that is by definition uncreated; asking who created it is like asking the bachelor's wife's name. If God had a creator, that creator would be God. Verses: 52:35-36; 112:1-4; 57:3. Sources: SeekersGuidance ; Islam Q&A 87677 . A2. “Why not an infinite chain of causes?” An infinite chain of dependent things is still a collection of dependent things; it cannot explain itself (the dominoes never fall without something that is not a domino). No actual infinite has ever been shown in nature, only in mathematics. Verse: 52:35-36. Source: Tzortzis, Divine Link . A3. “The universe came from nothing (quantum vacuum).” Lawrence Krauss's “nothing” is a quantum field with laws and energy, which is something. Absolute nothing has no properties and no power. Physicists' own critiques agree quantum-gravity models do not give “universes from nothing”. Verse: 52:35. Source: Tzortzis on Krauss . A4. “A multiverse explains fine-tuning.” A universe-generator must itself be finely tuned, so the problem moves up one level. Source: islamreligion.com, Fine-tuning part 7 . A5. “God of the gaps.” The dependency argument reasons from what science confirms (everything observed is contingent and began), not from ignorance. Al-Ghazali and al-Razi used it centuries before modern science, so it is not a retreat. Source: Tzortzis, Divine Link (above). A6. “The burden of proof is on you; atheism is just lack of belief.” Atheism is a claim about reality (no God) and carries a burden too; the idea that non-belief is the neutral default came from verificationism, which is itself unverifiable. Also, God-belief is the natural default (fitrah), so the one denying it must argue. Source: The Divine Reality , chapter 1; Yaqeen, Ibn Taymiyyah's critique . A7. “Extraordinary claims need extraordinary evidence.” A dependent universe that is uncaused, or arose from nothing, is at least as extraordinary. x: B1. The problem of evil. Yaqeen (Elshinawy; Hani): evil is “neither a logical nor a probabilistic objection to God's existence”. The logical version needs a hidden premise (God could have no good reason to permit evil) that cannot be proven; the evidential version assumes a limited human can judge what an all-wise being would permit. Islam's answer has layers: free will makes moral evil possible; life is a test (67:2, 2:155); suffering purifies, expiates sins and is compensated eternally; God's wisdom is not fully knowable (Khidr, 18:60-82); and the objection presupposes objective evil, which atheism cannot ground. Natural disasters. Theme C and D:
God's nature; science and religion
x: C1. “Why does God need worship? Is He egotistical, a dictator?” The verse after “I created jinn and men only to worship Me” (51:56) denies that God needs anything from us (51:57). Worship benefits the worshipper: it is gratitude to the One with all perfect attributes, and it frees the heart from worshipping lesser things (money, status, ego). A dictator extracts obedience for his own benefit; God commands what benefits us and gives free will to refuse (2:256). The “needy God” framing projects human psychology onto God. Verses: 51:56-57; 35:15; 14:8. Source: Yaqeen, Why does God ask for worship? . C2. “God's anger and jealousy are petty human emotions.” Muslims affirm God's attributes “in a manner that befits His majesty” without likening them to creatures (42:11). His anger is just displeasure at wrongdoing, which a perfectly good being must have; a God indifferent to oppression would be worse. “Jealousy” (ghayrah) in hadith means protectiveness over His rights and believers' honour, not insecurity. Verses: 42:11; 7:180. Source: Islamweb fatwa 38453 . D1. “Religion and science conflict.” The “conflict thesis” is a 19th-century story; Islamic civilisation founded observatories, hospitals and the scientific method (Ibn al-Haytham), and the Quran commands observation (2:164, 3:190-191, 96:1). Science answers how; revelation answers why and who. The dawah organisations now caution against over-claiming “scientific miracles”. Source: Yaqeen, Orientalists' fables about Islamic science . D2. “Evolution disproves Adam.” Yaqeen (Nazir Khan, Yasir Qadhi, David Jalajel): nothing in scripture denies mutation, natural selection, hominid species or common ancestry for other life; Adam's miraculous creation is a claim about one lineage, which empirical science (which studies regularities) cannot rule out. Evolutionary naturalism (unguided processes explain everything, including mind and morality) is a philosophical add-on that fails. A Muslim may accept the science and suspend judgement on how Adam fits. Verses: 3:59; 15:28-29; 71:14, 71:17. Sources: Human Origins I ; Human Origins II . D3. “The Quran says the earth is flat; seven heavens is primitive cosmology.” “Spread out” (15:19, 71:19) describes the surface from the human viewpoint; a carpet can be spread on a curved surface, and the Quran never says “flat”. Honest apologists reject Zakir Naik's “egg-shaped” reading of 79:30 as linguistically wrong. “Seven heavens” is idiom for completeness, not an astronomical mod

Theme E: The Quran and the
Prophet
x: E1. “Is the Quran reliably preserved?” Preserved by parallel mass memorisation and writing in the Prophet's lifetime; Abu Bakr's compilation checked each verse against written copies, memorisers and witnesses; Uthman's codex standardised the skeletal text; the minor regional readings (qira'at) strengthen rather than weaken the transmission. See the manuscripts table in the Evidence Library. Verses: 15:9; 75:17. Sources: Yaqeen, how the Quran was preserved ; The Uthmanic codex . E2. “The Quran contradicts itself.” The Quran invites the test (4:82). Apparent contradictions dissolve when one verse is general and another specific, or when Arabic usage is known (six days versus the “eight” of 41:9-12, which sum overlapping periods; who takes the soul, God through His angels). Ask the sceptic for the specific verse; most have never read one. E3. “Abrogation means God changed His mind.” Naskh replaces one ruling with a later one for a community in transition, not a truth with a falsehood; most cases (alcohol) are gradual restriction leading to prohibition. A doctor adjusting treatment is wisdom, not fickleness. Verses: 2:106; 16:101. Source: SeekersGuidance on naskh . E4. “Why Arabic? A universal God would speak to everyone.” Every messenger was sent in his people's language (14:4) so the first audience could understand and be accountable; any text must have one language. Arabic was then preserved because the Quran fixed it, allowing an unbroken 1,400-year reading. Translations carry the meaning; Islam does not require Arabic to accept the message, and Ma Jian's Chinese Quran exists for this reason. Verses: 14:4; 42:7; 41:44. Source: Why was the Quran revealed in Arabic? . E5. “The Quran was copied from the Bible.” The Quran retells shared stories to correct them (Adam, Jesus) and presents itself as confirming and guarding earlier revelation from the same God (5:48), so shared content is expected on its own thesis. Borrowing would require a literate, multilingual Prophet with Syriac and Hebrew texts in Mecca, which the record contradicts (29:48; 16:103). Source: Yaqeen, the Quran's engagement with Christian and Jewish literature . E6. “Muhammad wrote it himself.” He could not read or write and dictated to scribes; the Quran's style differs sharply from his own recorded speech (hadith); it rebukes him (80:1-10; 66:1); it contains knowledge he could not have had; and it challenged his enemies to produce its like (2:23), which they never did. Verses: 2:23; 29:48; 1

F1. “Islam oppresses women.” Islam introduced consent to marriage, the dower as the woman's own property, inheritance rights and spiritual equality (4:1; 33:35) in 7th-century Arabia. The inheritance difference tracks financial obligations (men must maintain women; women keep their wealth), and in many cases women inherit equally or more. The two-witness rule is limited to specific financial contracts. Hijab (24:30-31) begins with men lowering their gaze. Polygamy (4:3) is a restricted permission, not a command. Where women are mistreated, local culture is breaking Islamic law. Sources: Yaqeen, five myths about women in Islamic law ; Yaqeen, gender equity at the advent of Islam . F2. Slavery. Islam inherited a universal institution and radically regulated it: no enslavement of free people, humane treatment, equal food and clothing, no racial basis; emancipation was made an act of worship and the expiation for many sins (90:12-13; 24:33; 4:92; 5:89), so it came close to prohibition, and Muslim jurists approved abolition (Tunis, 1846). Freed slaves became leading scholars. Sources: Yaqeen, Slavery and Islam ; Mawali: how freed slaves shaped Islamic scholarship . F3. Apostasy. The Quran prescribes no earthly penalty for changing belief and affirms “no compulsion in religion” (2:256; 10:99; 18:29; 4:137). The classical penalty rests on hadith that many scholars (Shaltut, al-Qaradawi, Alalwani) read as targeting apostasy combined with treason in wartime; the Prophet never executed anyone for private loss of faith. Present it honestly as a debate among Muslims. Source: Yaqeen, the issue of apostasy . F4. Jihad and the “sword verse” (9:5). 9:1-7 concerns specific treaty-breaking pagans, and 9:6 commands protecting any who seek safety. Fighting is permitted only against aggression (2:190), under authority, with strict rules: never women, children, the elderly or anyone not fighting (Ibn Abbas; Abu Bakr's instructions). Islam spread in Indonesia, Malaysia and China by trade, not conquest; Muslims ruled India for centuries with a Hindu majority. Verses: 9:5-6; 2:190; 2:256; 5:32; 60:8. Source: Yaqeen, Is Islam a violent religion? . F5. “Religion causes war.” The Encyclopedia of Wars (Phillips and Axelrod) counts about 7% of 1,763 wars as primarily religious; the 20th century's secular and atheist regimes killed far more. Misuse by adherents does not refute a religion, any more than Stalin refutes atheism. In China, make the general point and do not discuss politics

The plan: one lesson per week, 30 minutes a day, alongside your normal HSK 3 and HSK 4 textbook (the lessons reuse HSK 3-4 vocabulary on purpose, so both reinforce each other). Day 1-2: learn the new words (write each character five times, say it aloud with tones). Day 3-4: learn the grammar patterns and copy the key sentences. Day 5: read the dialogue aloud, then cover the Chinese and translate from English. Day 6: say the sentences to a Chinese friend or a Hui Muslim and ask them to correct your tones. Day 7: go to Part I (the Dawah Handbook) and read the matching answer in Chinese. Tools: Pleco (dictionary with audio and flashcards, works in China), HelloChinese or Du Chinese (graded reading), and a Hui Muslim friend. Put every new word into Pleco flashcards. Tone marks: ā (1st, high flat), á (2nd, rising), ǎ (3rd, low dip), à (4th, falling). Tones are not optional: 主 zhǔ (Lord) and 猪 zhū (pig) differ only by tone. Grammar you need beyond HSK 2 You already know 是 , 有 , 吗 , 不 , 没有 , 了 , 的 , 很 , 也 , 都 , 可以 , 想 , 要 , 因为…所以 . These eight patterns carry almost every dawah sentence; each lesson practises one or two. Pattern Meaning বাংলা Example A 是 B 的 A is (description) B ক হলো (এমন) খ। উদাহরণ: ইসলাম যুক্তিসংগত। 伊斯兰是理性的。 Islam is rational. 如果…，就… if..., then... যদি…, তাহলে…। উদাহরণ: আল্লাহ না থাকলে ঠিক-ভুল বলে কিছু থাকে না। 如果没有真主，就没有对错。 If there is no God, there is no right and wrong. 不是…，而是… not..., but rather... …নয়, বরং…। উদাহরণ: আমি তোমাকে রাজি করাতে চাইছি না, বরং তোমার সঙ্গে একসাথে ভাবতে চাই। 我不是想说服你，而是想和你一起思考。 I am not trying to convince you, I want to think together. …不等于… ... does not equal ... …মানেই … নয়। উদাহরণ: জানা মানেই বাধ্য করা নয়। 知道不等于强迫。 Knowing is not forcing. 一定 must / certainly অবশ্যই / নিশ্চয়ই। উদাহরণ: যার শুরু আছে, তার অবশ্যই একটা কারণ আছে। 有开始的东西一定有原因。 What begins must have a cause. 就像…一样 just like... ঠিক …-এর মতো। উদাহরণ: ঠিক যেমন তুমি ডাক্তারকে বিশ্বাস করো। 就像你相信医生一样。 Just like you trust a doctor. 难道…吗？ surely it is not the case that...? Listen to this section · শুনুন Goal: Say who you are and what you need. Short, clear, friendly. Grammar you use here: 是 / 不 / 吗 / 的 / 想 + verb / 去 + place + verb # 汉字 Pinyin English বাংলা 1.1 我是穆斯林。 Wǒ shì Mù sī lín . I am a Muslim. আমি একজন মুসলিম। 1.2 我是学生，我在中国学习汉语。 Wǒ shì xué sheng , wǒ zài Zhōng guó xué xí Hàn yǔ . I am a student; I study Chinese in China. আমি ছাত্র, আমি চীনে চীনা ভাষা শিখি। 1.3 我的汉语不太好，对不起。 Wǒ de Hàn yǔ bú tài hǎo , duì bu qǐ . My Chinese is not very good, sorry. আমার চীনা ভাষা খুব ভালো না, দুঃখিত। 1.4 我不吃猪肉。我不喝酒。 Wǒ bù chī zhū ròu . Wǒ bù hē jiǔ . I don't eat pork. I don't drink alcohol. আমি শূকরের মাংস খাই না। আমি মদ পান করি না। 1.5 这个菜是清真的吗？ Zhè ge cài shì qīng zhēn de ma ? Is this dish halal? এই খাবারটা কি হালাল? 1.6 我想去清真饭店吃饭。 Wǒ xiǎng qù qīng zhēn fàn diàn chī fàn . I'd like to eat at a halal restaurant. আমি হালাল রেস্তোরাঁয় খেতে যেতে চাই। 1.7 你想喝茶吗？ Nǐ xiǎng hē chá ma ? Would you like some tea? তুমি কি চা খাবে? 1.8 对不起，我现在去礼拜。 Duì bu qǐ , wǒ xiàn zài qù lǐ bài . Sorry, I'm going to pray now. দুঃখিত, আমি এখন নামাজ পড়তে যাচ্ছি। 1.9 我去清真寺礼拜。 Wǒ qù qīng zhēn sì lǐ bài . I go to the mosque to pray. আমি মসজিদে নামাজ পড়তে যাই। 1.10 你想去清真寺看看吗？ Nǐ xiǎng qù qīng zhēn sì kàn kan ma ? Would you like to go and see a mosque? তুমি কি একটা মসজিদ দেখতে যেতে চাও? 1.11 我信真主。 Wǒ xìn Zhēn zhǔ . I believe in God. আমি আল্লাহকে বিশ্বাস করি। 1.12 你信什么宗教？ Nǐ xìn shén me zōng jiào ? What religion do you believe in? তুমি কোন ধর্মে বিশ্বাস করো? 1.13 真主创造了人。 Zhēn zhǔ chuàng zào le rén . God created people. আল্লাহ মানুষ সৃষ্টি করেছেন। 1.14 这是古兰经。 Zhè shì Gǔ lán jīng . This is the Quran. এটা কুরআন। 1.15 我很喜欢中国，中国人很好。 Wǒ hěn xǐ huan Zhōng guó , Zhōng guó rén hěn hǎo . I like China very much; Chinese people are very kind. আমি চীন খুব পছন্দ করি, চীনারা খুব ভালো। 1.16 谢谢你！我们是朋友。 Xiè xie nǐ ! Wǒ men shì péng you . Thank you! We are friends. ধন্যবাদ! আমরা বন্ধু। Practise: read each sentence aloud three times, cover the 汉字 column and say it from the English, then say it to a Muslim friend or record yourself. সারকথা: HSK 1 দিয়েই তুমি বলতে পারো তুমি মুসলিম, হালাল খাবার চাইতে পারো, আর নামাজে যাওয়ার কথা ভদ্রভাবে জানাতে পারো।

Listen to this section · শুনুন Goal: Add 因为…所以… , 虽然…但是… , and ask your friend a big question. Grammar you use here: 因为…所以… / 虽然…但是… / 过 (experience) / 一起…吧 # 汉字 Pinyin English বাংলা 2.1 因为我是穆斯林，所以我不吃猪肉。 Yīn wèi wǒ shì Mù sī lín , suǒ yǐ wǒ bù chī zhū ròu . Because I am a Muslim, I don't eat pork. যেহেতু আমি মুসলিম, তাই আমি শূকরের মাংস খাই না। 2.2 我一天礼拜五次。 Wǒ yì tiān lǐ bài wǔ cì . I pray five times a day. আমি দিনে পাঁচবার নামাজ পড়ি। 2.3 每次礼拜五分钟就好。 Měi cì lǐ bài wǔ fēn zhōng jiù hǎo . Each prayer takes just five minutes. প্রতিবার নামাজে পাঁচ মিনিট হলেই হয়। 2.4 我礼拜前要洗手。 Wǒ lǐ bài qián yào xǐ shǒu . I wash my hands before prayer. আমি নামাজের আগে হাত ধুই। 2.5 你想过这个问题吗？我们从哪儿来？ Nǐ xiǎng guo zhè ge wèn tí ma ? Wǒ men cóng nǎ r lái ? Have you thought about this question: where do we come from? তুমি কি এই প্রশ্নটা ভেবেছ? আমরা কোথা থেকে এসেছি? 2.6 我们到哪儿去？ Wǒ men dào nǎ r qù ? Where are we going? আমরা কোথায় যাচ্ছি? 2.7 你知道吗？中国有很多穆斯林。 Nǐ zhī dào ma ? Zhōng guó yǒu hěn duō Mù sī lín . Did you know? China has many Muslims. তুমি কি জানো? চীনে অনেক মুসলিম আছে। 2.8 虽然我的汉语不太好，但是我很想和你说说。 Suī rán wǒ de Hàn yǔ bú tài hǎo , dàn shì wǒ hěn xiǎng hé nǐ shuō shuo . Although my Chinese isn't good, I'd really like to talk with you. যদিও আমার চীনা ভাষা ভালো না, তবুও আমি তোমার সাথে কথা বলতে চাই। 2.9 这个问题很有意思。 Zhè ge wèn tí hěn yǒu yì si . This question is very interesting. এই প্রশ্নটা খুব মজার। 2.10 我们一起去清真寺吧！ Wǒ men yì qǐ qù qīng zhēn sì ba ! Let's go to the mosque together! চলো একসাথে মসজিদে যাই! 2.11 真主没有孩子，也没有爸爸妈妈。 Zhēn zhǔ méi yǒu hái zi , yě méi yǒu bà ba mā ma . God has no children and no parents. আল্লাহর কোনো সন্তান নেই, বাবা-মাও নেই। 2.12 真主没有开始，没有人创造他。 Zhēn zhǔ méi yǒu kāi shǐ , méi yǒu rén chuàng zào tā . God has no beginning; no one created Him. আল্লাহর কোনো শুরু নেই, কেউ তাঁকে সৃষ্টি করেনি। 2.13 你可以问我问题，没关系。 Nǐ kě yǐ wèn wǒ wèn tí , méi guān xi . You can ask me questions, no problem. তুমি আমাকে প্রশ্ন করতে পারো, কোনো অসুবিধা নেই। 2.14 我希望你能来我家吃饭。 Wǒ xī wàng nǐ néng lái wǒ jiā chī fàn . I hope you can come to my home for a meal. আমি আশা করি তুমি আমার বাসায় খেতে আসবে। 2.15 先知说：笑也是好事。 Xiān zhī shuō : xiào yě shì hǎo shì . The Prophet said: a smile is also a good deed. নবী বলেছেন: হাসিও একটি ভালো কাজ। 2.16 我不知道，我回去问问，再告诉你。 Wǒ bù zhī dào , wǒ huí qu wèn wen , zài gào su nǐ . Listen to this section · শুনুন Goal: Explain one God, the creator, the hereafter and Ramadan in simple sentences. Grammar you use here: 如果…的话 / 只有… / 已经…了 / …以后 / 对…有兴趣 # 汉字 Pinyin English বাংলা 3.1 我相信宇宙有一个创造者。 Wǒ xiāng xìn yǔ zhòu yǒu yí ge chuàng zào zhě . I believe the universe has a Creator. আমি বিশ্বাস করি মহাবিশ্বের একজন স্রষ্টা আছেন। 3.2 世界上的东西都有开始，宇宙也有开始。 Shì jiè shang de dōng xi dōu yǒu kāi shǐ , yǔ zhòu yě yǒu kāi shǐ . Everything in the world has a beginning; the universe has one too. পৃথিবীর সবকিছুর শুরু আছে, মহাবিশ্বেরও শুরু আছে। 3.3 如果没有创造者，宇宙是从哪儿来的？ Rú guǒ méi yǒu chuàng zào zhě , yǔ zhòu shì cóng nǎ r lái de ? If there is no Creator, where did the universe come from? যদি কোনো স্রষ্টা না থাকেন, তাহলে মহাবিশ্ব কোথা থেকে এল? 3.4 伊斯兰教很简单：只有一个真主。 Yī sī lán jiào hěn jiǎn dān : zhǐ yǒu yí ge Zhēn zhǔ . Islam is simple: there is only one God. ইসলাম খুব সহজ: আল্লাহ একজনই। 3.5 我们只崇拜真主，不崇拜偶像。 Wǒ men zhǐ chóng bài Zhēn zhǔ , bù chóng bài ǒu xiàng . We worship only God, not idols. আমরা শুধু আল্লাহর ইবাদত করি, মূর্তির নয়। 3.6 其实，伊斯兰教在中国已经一千三百多年了。 Qí shí , Yī sī lán jiào zài Zhōng guó yǐ jīng yì qiān sān bǎi duō nián le . Actually, Islam has been in China for over 1,300 years. আসলে ইসলাম চীনে ১৩০০ বছরেরও বেশি সময় ধরে আছে। 3.7 我们认为，这个世界是一个考验。 Wǒ men rèn wéi , zhè ge shì jiè shì yí ge kǎo yàn . We believe this world is a test. আমরা মনে করি, এই দুনিয়া একটা পরীক্ষা। 3.8 人离开这个世界以后，还有后世。 Rén lí kāi zhè ge shì jiè yǐ hòu , hái yǒu hòu shì . After a person leaves this world, there is still the afterlife. মানুষ এই দুনিয়া ছেড়ে যাওয়ার পরেও আখিরাত আছে। 3.9 古兰经说：要对爸爸妈妈好。 Gǔ lán jīng shuō : yào duì bà ba mā ma hǎo . The Quran says: be good to your parents. কুরআন বলে: বাবা-মায়ের প্রতি ভালো ব্যবহার করো। 3.10 斋月的时候，我们白天不吃也不喝。 Zhāi yuè de shí hou , wǒ men bái tiān bù chī yě bù hē . During Ramadan we don't eat or drink in the daytime. রমজানে আমরা দিনের বেলা খাই না, পানও করি না। 3.11 头巾是她自己的选择。 Tóu jīn shì tā zì jǐ de xuǎn zé . The headscarf is her own choice. হিজাব তার নিজের পছন্দ। 3.12 信不信是你自己的选择。 Xìn bu xìn shì nǐ zì jǐ de xuǎn zé . Whether you believe or not is your own choice. বিশ্বাস করবে কি না, সেটা তোমার নিজের সিদ্ধান্ত। 3.13 先知穆罕默德是最后一个使者。 Xiān zhī Mù hǎn mò dé shì zuì hòu yí ge shǐ zhě . The Prophet Muhammad is the last messenger. নবী মুহাম্মদ সর্বশেষ রাসূল। 3.14 你对这个有兴趣的话，可以看看中文的古兰经。 Nǐ duì zhè ge yǒu xìng qù de huà , kě yǐ kàn kan Zhōng wén de Gǔ lán jīng . If you are interested, you can read the Quran in Chinese. তোমার আগ্রহ থাকলে চীনা ভাষার কুরআন পড়ে

Listen to this section · শুনুন Goal: Give a short argument ( 既然…就… , 不但…而且… , 只要…就… ) and stay friendly when you disagree. Grammar you use here: 既然…就… / 不但…而且… / 无论…都… / 只要…就… / 不等于 # 汉字 Pinyin English বাংলা 4.1 既然宇宙有开始，它就一定有原因。 Jì rán yǔ zhòu yǒu kāi shǐ , tā jiù yí dìng yǒu yuán yīn . Since the universe has a beginning, it must have a cause. মহাবিশ্বের যেহেতু শুরু আছে, তাই এর অবশ্যই একটা কারণ আছে। 4.2 科学能解释宇宙是怎么样的，但是不能解释宇宙为什么存在。 Kē xué néng jiě shì yǔ zhòu shì zěn me yàng de , dàn shì bù néng jiě shì yǔ zhòu wèi shén me cún zài . Science can explain what the universe is like, but not why it exists. বিজ্ঞান ব্যাখ্যা করতে পারে মহাবিশ্ব কেমন, কিন্তু কেন আছে তা ব্যাখ্যা করতে পারে না। 4.3 伊斯兰教不但不反对科学，而且鼓励科学。 Yī sī lán jiào bú dàn bù fǎn duì kē xué , ér qiě gǔ lì kē xué . Each sentence was split into words with the jieba segmenter. A word passes if (a) it is in the list at or below the sentence's level, (b) it is a Dawah Core Word of the right tier (VI.2), (c) it is a number, or (d) it is a short compound made only of characters you already know at that level (for example 等于 at HSK 4). h: D.1 The HSK exams at a glance
p: Appendix D: HSK Grammar & Exam Guide
x: Listen to this section · শুনুন The table shows the HSK 2.0 written exams, the format used for many years and the one most textbooks and past papers follow. Level Listening Reading Writing Questions Total time Total score Pass mark Words HSK 1 20 questions, about 15 min 20 questions, 17 min none 40 about 40 min 200 120 150 HSK 2 35 questions, about 25 min 25 questions, 22 min none 60 about 55 min 200 120 300 HSK 3 40 questions, about 35 min 30 questions, 30 min 10 questions, 15 min 80 about 90 min 300 180 600 HSK 4 45 questions, about 30 min 40 questions, 40 min 15 questions, 25 min 100 about 105 min 300 180 1,200 Reading the table. Total time includes about 5 minutes for writing your personal details on the answer sheet. Score: each section is worth 100 points. The pass mark is for the total score. Words are cumulative: HSK 4 means all 1,200 words of HSK 1–4. Your app list in Appendix C has 1,089 of them (see VI.15). Pinyin: HSK 1 and HSK 2 papers print pinyin with the characters. From HSK 3 there is no pinyin , so you must read characters. Writing, HSK 3: put given words in the right order to make a sentence (5 questions); write the missing character from its pinyin (5 questions). Writing, HSK 4: put given words in the right order (10 questions); look at a picture and write one sentence with a given word (5 questions). Listening: in HSK 1–3 each recording is usually played twice; in HSK 4 only once. (Check this in the official sample paper for your level.) Speaking is not part of the HSK. The speaking test is a separate exam called HSKK . Many universities ask for both, so check your admission letter. Not given here because they change: fees, test dates, and how long a score is accepted. Many universities accept a score for two years, but check with yours.  The exam is changing: check before you book. China has a new standard for Chinese tests, often called HSK 3.0 , with nine levels in three bands. It is being introduced in stages. The new tests use larger word lists and may have different parts, timings and pass marks from the table above. Before you register, check the current format, word list, test dates, fees and registration on the official site chinesetest.cn , and ask your university's international office which version they accept. বুক করার আগে দেখে নাও: HSK-এর নতুন মান (HSK 3.0, তিন ধাপে নয়টা লেভেল) ধীরে ধীরে চালু হচ্ছে। নতুন পরীক্ষায় শব্দ বেশি, আর অংশ, সময় ও পাস নম্বর ওপরের টেবিল থেকে আলাদা হতে পারে। রেজিস্ট্রেশনের আগে অফিশিয়াল সাইট chin

p: Appendix D: HSK Grammar & Exam Guide
x: Listen to this section · শুনুন HSK 1 has listening and reading only, with pinyin on the paper. These patterns make almost every sentence in it, and Stage 1 of Part VI (VI.3) uses the same grammar. Words allowed in the examples: HSK 1 + Tier 1 Dawah Core Words. D.2.1 A 是 B Use: links two nouns: "A is B". Do not put 是 before an adjective (say 我很好 , not 我是好 ). ব্যবহার: দুটো বিশেষ্যকে জোড়া দেয়: "A হলো B"; বিশেষণের আগে 是 বসে না ( 我很好 বলো, 我是好 নয়)। 汉字 Pinyin English বাংলা 我是穆斯林。 Wǒ shì Mù sī lín . I am a Muslim. আমি একজন মুসলিম। 我朋友是中国人。 Wǒ péng you shì Zhōng guó rén . My friend is Chinese. আমার বন্ধু চীনা। D.2.2 有 and 没有 Use: 有 means "to have" or "there is"; its negative is always 没有 , never 不有 . ব্যবহার: 有 মানে "আছে"; এর না-বাচক সবসময় 没有 , কখনো 不有 নয়। 汉字 Pinyin English বাংলা 学校前面有一个清真饭店。 Xué xiào qián miàn yǒu yí ge qīng zhēn fàn diàn . There is a halal restaurant in front of the campus. ক্যাম্পাসের সামনে একটা হালাল রেস্তোরাঁ আছে। 这个菜没有猪肉。 Zhè ge cài méi yǒu zhū ròu . This dish has no pork. এই খাবারে শূকরের মাংস নেই। D.2.3 Statement + 吗？ Use: put 吗 at the end of a statement to make a yes/no question; the word order does not change. ব্যবহার: বাক্যের শেষে 吗 বসালে হ্যাঁ/না প্রশ্ন হয়; শব্দের ক্রম বদলায় না। 汉字 Pinyin English বাংলা 你是穆斯林吗？ Nǐ shì Mù sī lín ma ? Are you a Muslim? তুমি কি মুসলিম? 你喜欢喝茶吗？ Nǐ xǐ huan hē chá ma ? Do you like tea? তুমি কি চা পছন্দ করো? D.2.4 Noun + 呢？ Use: after a noun or pronoun, 呢 asks "and … ?" or "where is … ?" ব্যবহার: বিশেষ্য বা সর্বনামের পরে 呢 মানে "আর … ?" বা " … কোথায়?" 汉字 Pinyin English বাংলা 我是孟加拉国人，你呢？ Wǒ shì Mèng jiā lā guó rén , nǐ ne ? I'm from Bangladesh. And you? আমি বাংলাদেশি, আর তুমি? 我的古兰经呢？ Wǒ de Gǔ lán jīng ne ? Where is my Quran? আমার কুরআনটা কোথায়? D.2.5 的 : possession and description Use: 的 joins a describer to a noun ( 我的书 my book); with close family it is often left out ( 我妈妈 ). ব্যবহার: 的 দিয়ে "এর/র" বোঝায় ( 我的书 আমার বই); কাছের আত্মীয়ের বেলায় প্রায়ই বাদ পড়ে ( 我妈妈 )। 汉字 Pinyin English বাংলা 这是我的古兰经。 Zhè shì wǒ de Gǔ lán jīng . This is my Quran. এটা আমার কুরআন। 我们学校的饭店有清真菜。 Wǒ men xué xiào de fàn diàn yǒu qīng zhēn cài . Our campus restaurant has halal food. আমাদের ক্যাম্পাসের রেস্তোরাঁয় হালাল খাবার আছে। D.2.6 不 + verb or adjective Use: 不 negates the present, the future and habits. Tone: 不 is bù, but bú before a 4th tone ( 不是 bú shì). ব্যবহার: 不 দিয়ে বর্তমান, ভবিষ্যৎ ও অভ্যাসের "না" বোঝায়; ৪র্থ টোনের আগে 不 হয় bú ( 不是 bú shì)। 汉字 Pinyin English বাংলা 我不吃猪肉。 Wǒ bù chī zhū ròu . I don't eat pork

p: Appendix D: HSK Grammar & Exam Guide
x: Listen to this section · শুনুন HSK 2 adds aspect ( 过 , 着 , 正在 ), comparison with 比 , and the first two-part connectors. Stage 2 of Part VI (VI.4) uses them. Words allowed in the examples: HSK 1–2 + Tier 1 Dawah Core Words. Two pattern words are listed higher in your app: 得 (de) is an official HSK 2 word but your app lists it at HSK 4, and 或者 is an HSK 3 word shown here only to contrast it with 还是 . D.3.1 Verb + 过 (experience) Use: 过 after a verb means "have (ever) done"; the negative is 没 + verb + 过 . ব্যবহার: ক্রিয়ার পরে 过 মানে "কখনো করেছি" (অভিজ্ঞতা); না-বাচক 没 + ক্রিয়া + 过 । 汉字 Pinyin English বাংলা 你去过清真寺吗？ Nǐ qù guo qīng zhēn sì ma ? Have you ever been to a mosque? তুমি কি কখনো মসজিদে গেছ? 我没看过古兰经。 Wǒ méi kàn guo Gǔ lán jīng . I have never read the Quran. আমি কখনো কুরআন পড়িনি। D.3.2 Verb + 着 (continuing state) Use: 着 after a verb shows a state that continues ( 门开着 ), or one action going on while another happens ( 笑着说 ). ব্যবহার: ক্রিয়ার পরে 着 মানে অবস্থাটা চলছে ( 门开着 দরজা খোলা), বা এক কাজ করতে করতে আরেক কাজ ( 笑着说 হেসে বলা)। 汉字 Pinyin English বাংলা 门开着，你进来吧。 Mén kāi zhe , nǐ jìn lai ba . The door is open, come in. দরজা খোলা আছে, ভেতরে এসো। 他笑着说：“没关系。” Tā xiào zhe shuō : " Méi guān xi ." He said with a smile, "It's fine." সে হেসে বলল, "কোনো সমস্যা নেই।" D.3.3 正在 + verb (+ 呢 ) Use: 正在 before a verb (often with 呢 at the end) means "in the middle of doing". ব্যবহার: ক্রিয়ার আগে 正在 (প্রায়ই শেষে 呢 ) মানে "এখন করছে"। 汉字 Pinyin English বাংলা 他正在礼拜呢，请你等一下。 Tā zhèng zài lǐ bài ne , qǐng nǐ děng yí xià . He is praying right now; please wait a moment. সে এখন নামাজ পড়ছে, একটু অপেক্ষা করো। 我们正在吃饭，你也来吧！ Wǒ men zhèng zài chī fàn , nǐ yě lái ba ! We're eating now; come and join us! আমরা এখন খাচ্ছি, তুমিও এসো! D.3.4 要…了 and 快…了 Use: 要 / 快 + verb + 了 means something is about to happen. ব্যবহার: 要 / 快 + ক্রিয়া + 了 মানে কিছু একটা এখনই ঘটতে যাচ্ছে। 汉字 Pinyin English বাংলা 要礼拜了，我去洗手。 Yào lǐ bài le , wǒ qù xǐ shǒu . It's nearly prayer time; I'm going to wash my hands. নামাজের সময় হয়ে এল, আমি হাত ধুতে যাচ্ছি। 快考试了，我们一起准备吧。 Kuài kǎo shì le , wǒ men yì qǐ zhǔn bèi ba . The exam is coming soon; let's prepare together. পরীক্ষা চলে এসেছে, চলো একসাথে প্রস্তুতি নিই। D.3.5 A 比 B + adjective Use: A 比 B + adjective = "A is more … than B"; do not put 很 before the adjective. The negative is A 没有 B + adjective. ব্যবহার: A 比 B + বিশেষণ = "A, B-এর চেয়ে বেশি … "; তখন 很 বসে না। না-বাচক: A 没有 B + বিশেষণ। 汉字 Pinyin English বাংলা 今天比昨天冷。 Jīn tiān bǐ zuó tiān lěng . Today is colder tha

p: Appendix D: HSK Grammar & Exam Guide
x: Listen to this section · শুনুন HSK 3 is the first level with a writing part and no pinyin. The word-order questions test 把 , 被 , complements and the connectors below again and again. Stage 3 of Part VI (VI.5) and the first lessons of Part V use them. Words allowed in the examples: HSK 1–3 + Tier 1–2 Dawah Core Words. D.4.1 把 + object + verb + result Use: 把 brings a definite object before the verb to say what you do to it; the verb must be followed by a result or a place. ব্যবহার: 把 দিয়ে নির্দিষ্ট কর্মকে ক্রিয়ার আগে আনা হয়, জিনিসটার সাথে কী করা হলো তা বোঝাতে; ক্রিয়ার পরে ফল বা জায়গা থাকতেই হবে। 汉字 Pinyin English বাংলা 请把鞋放在门外。 Qǐng bǎ xié fàng zài mén wài . Please leave your shoes outside the door. দয়া করে জুতা দরজার বাইরে রাখো। 我把古兰经放在桌子上。 Wǒ bǎ Gǔ lán jīng fàng zài zhuō zi shang . I put the Quran on the table. আমি কুরআনটা টেবিলের উপর রাখলাম। D.4.2 被 (passive) Use: subject + 被 (+ doer) + verb + result: something happens to the subject, often something unwanted. ব্যবহার: 被 দিয়ে কর্মবাচ্য হয়: কর্তার উপর কিছু ঘটে, প্রায়ই অপ্রত্যাশিত কিছু। 汉字 Pinyin English বাংলা 我的伞被朋友借走了。 Wǒ de sǎn bèi péng you jiè zǒu le . My umbrella was borrowed by a friend. আমার ছাতাটা এক বন্ধু ধার নিয়ে গেছে। 这个问题已经被他解决了。 Zhè ge wèn tí yǐ jīng bèi tā jiě jué le . This problem has already been solved by him. এই সমস্যাটা সে ইতিমধ্যে সমাধান করে ফেলেছে। D.4.3 比较 + adjective Use: 比较 before an adjective means "fairly" or "rather"; it does not need a second thing to compare with. ব্যবহার: বিশেষণের আগে 比较 মানে "তুলনামূলক / বেশ"; এখানে আরেকটা জিনিসের সাথে তুলনা লাগে না। 汉字 Pinyin English বাংলা 清真寺附近的饭店比较便宜。 Qīng zhēn sì fù jìn de fàn diàn bǐ jiào pián yi . The restaurants near the mosque are fairly cheap. মসজিদের আশেপাশের রেস্তোরাঁগুলো তুলনামূলক সস্তা। 这个问题比较难。 Zhè ge wèn tí bǐ jiào nán . This question is rather difficult. এই প্রশ্নটা বেশ কঠিন। D.4.4 越来越 and 越…越… Use: 越来越 + adjective = "more and more"; 越 A 越 B = "the more A, the more B". ব্যবহার: 越来越 + বিশেষণ = "দিন দিন আরও"; 越 A 越 B = "যত A, তত B"। 汉字 Pinyin English বাংলা 我的汉语越来越好了。 Wǒ de Hàn yǔ yuè lái yuè hǎo le . My Chinese is getting better and better. আমার চীনা ভাষা দিন দিন ভালো হচ্ছে। 我越了解宇宙，越相信有创造者。 Wǒ yuè liǎo jiě yǔ zhòu , yuè xiāng xìn yǒu chuàng zào zhě . The more I understand the universe, the more I believe there is a Creator. মহাবিশ্বকে যত বুঝি, তত বেশি বিশ্বাস করি যে একজন স্রষ্টা আছেন। D.4.5 一边…，一边… Use: two actions done at the same time by the same person. ব্যবহার: একই মানুষ একসাথে দুটো কাজ করছে: "… করতে করতে …"। 汉字 P

p: Appendix D: HSK Grammar & Exam Guide
x: Listen to this section · শুনুন HSK 4 grammar is mostly about connectors : words that join two clauses and show how they relate. In the writing part you reorder words into a sentence, and these connectors are the main clue. Stage 4 of Part VI (VI.6) and Lessons 3–11 of Part V use them in arguments. Words allowed in the examples: HSK 1–4 + all Dawah Core Words. 连 is not in your app's word list; it is used here as the pattern being taught. D.5.1 既然…，就… Use: 既然 states a fact both speakers accept, and 就 gives the conclusion; it is different from 如果 , which only supposes. ব্যবহার: 既然 এমন সত্য বলে যা দুজনেই মানে, আর 就 দিয়ে সিদ্ধান্ত আসে; 如果 (যদি) শুধু ধরে নেয়, তাই আলাদা। 汉字 Pinyin English বাংলা 既然你有兴趣，我们就一起去清真寺参观吧。 Jì rán nǐ yǒu xìng qù , wǒ men jiù yì qǐ qù qīng zhēn sì cān guān ba . Since you're interested, let's visit the mosque together. তোমার যেহেতু আগ্রহ আছে, চলো একসাথে মসজিদটা ঘুরে দেখি। 既然下雨了，我们就在家复习吧。 Jì rán xià yǔ le , wǒ men jiù zài jiā fù xí ba . Since it's raining, let's revise at home. বৃষ্টি যেহেতু হচ্ছেই, চলো বাসায় পড়া রিভিশন দিই। D.5.2 不但…，而且… Use: "not only …, but also …"; the second part adds something stronger. ব্যবহার: "শুধু … নয়, … ও"; দ্বিতীয় অংশে আরও জোরালো কিছু যোগ হয়। 汉字 Pinyin English বাংলা 他不但会说汉语，而且会读阿拉伯语。 Tā bú dàn huì shuō Hàn yǔ , ér qiě huì dú Ā lā bó yǔ . He not only speaks Chinese, he can also read Arabic. সে শুধু চীনা বলতেই পারে না, আরবিও পড়তে পারে। 礼拜不但让心安静，而且让人按时起床。 Lǐ bài bú dàn ràng xīn ān jìng , ér qiě ràng rén àn shí qǐ chuáng . Prayer not only calms the heart, it also gets you up on time. নামাজ শুধু মনকে শান্তই করে না, সময়মতো ঘুম থেকে উঠতেও সাহায্য করে। D.5.3 无论…，都… Use: 无论 + a question word or "A 不 A", then 都 = "no matter … "; in speech people often say 不管 . ব্যবহার: 无论 + প্রশ্নবোধক শব্দ বা "A 不 A", তারপর 都 = "যা-ই হোক না কেন"; মুখের ভাষায় প্রায়ই 不管 । 汉字 Pinyin English বাংলা 无论多忙，他每天都礼拜五次。 Wú lùn duō máng , tā měi tiān dōu lǐ bài wǔ cì . No matter how busy he is, he prays five times every day. যত ব্যস্তই থাকুক, সে প্রতিদিন পাঁচ ওয়াক্ত নামাজ পড়ে। 无论你信不信，我们都是朋友。 Wú lùn nǐ xìn bu xìn , wǒ men dōu shì péng you . Whether you believe or not, we are friends. তুমি বিশ্বাস করো বা না করো, আমরা বন্ধুই। D.5.4 即使…，也… Use: "even if …, still …": a supposed situation that does not change the result. ব্যবহার: "এমনকি … হলেও …": একটা ধরে নেওয়া অবস্থা, তবুও ফল বদলায় না। 汉字 Pinyin English বাংলা 即使很累，他也坚持早上礼拜。 Jí shǐ hěn lèi , tā yě jiān chí zǎo shang lǐ bài . Even when he is tired, he keeps up the morning prayer. খুব ক্লান্

Listen to this section · শুনুন # 汉字 Pinyin English বাংলা 1 我是穆斯林。 Wǒ shì Mù sī lín . I am a Muslim. আমি একজন মুসলিম। 2 我不吃猪肉。我不喝酒。 Wǒ bù chī zhū ròu . Wǒ bù hē jiǔ . I don't eat pork. I don't drink alcohol. আমি শূকরের মাংস খাই না। আমি মদ পান করি না। 3 这个菜是清真的吗？ Zhè ge cài shì qīng zhēn de ma ? Is this dish halal? এই খাবারটা কি হালাল? 4 对不起，我现在去礼拜。 Duì bu qǐ , wǒ xiàn zài qù lǐ bài . Sorry, I'm going to pray now. দুঃখিত, আমি এখন নামাজ পড়তে যাচ্ছি। 5 因为我是穆斯林，所以我不吃猪肉。 Yīn wèi wǒ shì Mù sī lín , suǒ yǐ wǒ bù chī zhū ròu . Because I am a Muslim, I don't eat pork. যেহেতু আমি মুসলিম, তাই আমি শূকরের মাংস খাই না। 6 你想过这个问题吗？我们从哪儿来？ Nǐ xiǎng guo zhè ge wèn tí ma ? Wǒ men cóng nǎ r lái ? Have you thought about this question: where do we come from? তুমি কি এই প্রশ্নটা ভেবেছ? আমরা কোথা থেকে এসেছি? 7 真主没有开始，没有人创造他。 Zhēn zhǔ méi yǒu kāi shǐ , méi yǒu rén chuàng zào tā . God has no beginning; no one created Him. আল্লাহর কোনো শুরু নেই, কেউ তাঁকে সৃষ্টি করেনি। 8 我相信宇宙有一个创造者。 Wǒ xiāng xìn yǔ zhòu yǒu yí ge chuàng zào zhě . I believe the universe has a Creator. আমি বিশ্বাস করি মহাবিশ্বের একজন স্রষ্টা আছেন। 9 信不信是你自己的选择。 Xìn bu xìn shì nǐ zì jǐ de xuǎn zé . Whether you believe or not is your own choice. বিশ্বাস করবে কি না, সেটা তোমার নিজের সিদ্ধান্ত। 10 我不知道，我回去问问，再告诉你。 Wǒ bù zhī dào , wǒ huí qu wèn wen , zài gào su nǐ . I don't know; I'll go back, ask, and tell you. আমি জানি না, আমি জিজ্ঞেস করে তোমাকে পরে বলব। 11 我尊重你的选择，我们永远是朋友。 Wǒ zūn zhòng nǐ de xuǎn zé , wǒ men yǒng yuǎn shì péng you . I respect your choice; we will always be friends. আমি তোমার সিদ্ধান্তকে সম্মান করি, আমরা সবসময় বন্ধু থাকব। 12 你可以问我问题，没关系。 Nǐ kě yǐ wèn wǒ wèn tí , méi guān xi . You can ask me questions, no problem. তুমি আমাকে প্রশ্ন করতে পারো, কোনো অসুবিধা নেই। সারকথা: এই ১২টা বাক্য দিয়েই প্রথম পরিচয় থেকে বড় প্রশ্ন পর্যন্ত কথা চালানো যায়। প্রতিদিন একবার জোরে বলো।

Listen to this section · শুনুন Answer, do not preach. Talk about faith when a friend asks; never in public, never online for Chinese audiences, never by handing out material. বাংলা বন্ধু জিজ্ঞেস করলে উত্তর দাও; প্রকাশ্যে, অনলাইনে বা লিফলেট দিয়ে প্রচার নয়। No politics. 对不起，我是学生，我不太了解政治。我们聊别的吧。 (Duìbuqǐ, wǒ shì xuésheng, wǒ bú tài liǎojiě zhèngzhì. Wǒmen liáo bié de ba.) Sorry, I'm a student and don't really understand politics. Let's talk about something else. বাংলা দুঃখিত, আমি ছাত্র, রাজনীতি খুব একটা বুঝি না। চলো অন্য কিছু নিয়ে কথা বলি। Refer, do not recruit. If a friend wants to learn more, take them to the ahong of a registered mosque: 我带你去清真寺见阿訇吧。 (Wǒ dài nǐ qù qīngzhēnsì jiàn āhōng ba.) Let me take you to the mosque to meet the imam. বাংলা চলো তোমাকে মসজিদে ইমামের কাছে নিয়ে যাই। সারকথা: উত্তর দাও, প্রচার নয়; রাজনীতি নয়; আগ্রহী হলে নিবন্ধিত মসজিদের আহং-এর কাছে নিয়ে যাও। এই তিন নিয়মে তুমি আর তোমার বন্ধু দুজনেই নিরাপদ।
